name: Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) rebellion in northern Mali
started: 2026-04-25 (joint FLA-JNIM offensive; the Tuareg rebellion resumed in 2023)
summary: Tuareg separatists of the FLA, openly allied with JNIM since April 2026, took Kidal and forced Malian and Russian troops out of much of the far north, then fought a seesaw summer campaign around Anefis. On 6 Oct 2026 a Malian and Africa Corps convoy reoccupied Kidal after the FLA pulled out, citing air strikes. The town is symbolic: Russia's 2023 capture of Kidal was the junta's showcase victory.

sides.name: Azawad Liberation Front (FLA)
members: Tactical partner: JNIM (joint operations openly confirmed in April 2026)
backers: No state backer documented in sources found
sides.strength: No reliable figure found; Africa Corps claimed 10,000-12,000 JNIM and FLA fighters joined the April offensive (unverified).

background: Northern Mali (Azawad to the separatists) has seen Tuareg rebellions since independence. The 2015 Algiers peace deal collapsed after the UN mission left in 2023; the junta, with Wagner, then retook Kidal in November 2023 and scrapped the accord. Tuareg factions regrouped and merged into the FLA, whose first big success was the Anoumalane ambush on 13 June 2025 that killed about 45 Malian and Russian personnel, Africa Corps' first major defeat after replacing Wagner.

The key change in 2026 is that the secular-separatist FLA and al-Qaeda's JNIM publicly confirmed joint operations for the first time in the war, and agreed a softer local form of sharia in FLA areas. Why it matters: the alliance combines FLA's local legitimacy and desert mobility with JNIM's numbers and explosives, and it reversed Russia's only real battlefield gains in Mali.
year: On 25 April 2026 FLA and JNIM fighters entered Kidal at dawn; checkpoints changed hands within an hour and the FLA took the governor's residence while Gen. Ag Gamou sheltered in the former UN camp. By 26-27 April Malian and Russian troops left Kidal under an FLA-negotiated deal with Algerian mediation, and then left Aguelhok and Tessalit; FLA and JNIM took the Tessalit base on 1 May. Gao city was largely in rebel hands while FAMa held its airport. The army bombed Kidal with drones and Su-24s on 27 May, damaging FLA leader Bilal Ag Acherif's home.

On 4 July the FLA renewed its offensive, took most of Anefis in about two hours and besieged the base; a relief column was routed at Tabrichat on 5 July and a Mi-24 was shot down. A second FAMa-Africa Corps convoy retook Anefis on 9 July. The FLA ambushed a convoy returning from Anefis on 17 July, killing about 50 soldiers and capturing 20 (RFI). In August the FLA released 82 Malian prisoners and later about 60 more in exchange for one of its generals. After weeks of air strikes, about 120 vehicles of FAMa, Africa Corps, GATIA and MSA drove from Anefis to Kidal on 6 Oct and entered the town without major ground combat after the FLA announced a 'strategic and controlled withdrawal'.
situation: Kidal town is back under Malian and Russian control as of 6 Oct 2026, but the FLA says the pullback is temporary and it keeps its forces intact. Analysts call the recapture symbolic rather than decisive (Control Risks via Reuters). Government forces hold bases at Anefis and Kidal and Gao airport, while ACLED analysts note they did not control the terrain around Anefis or the supply corridor; FLA and JNIM remain active in the Adrar des Ifoghas, around Tessalit-Aguelhok and on the RN18 corridor.
technical: Kidal fell in under 48 hours on 25-27 April 2026; Africa Corps confirmed its withdrawal around 27 April after Algerian mediation (France 24 via Wikipedia).
Negotiated weapons-for-safe-passage withdrawals by Malian and Russian forces from Tessit, Ber, Lere and the Intahaka gold mine; Labbezanga abandoned to ISSP (Wikipedia; Critical Threats).
Bourem and Gao sit on the RN18 north-south road and the RN33/RN16 east-west junctions; holding them cut Malian and Russian reinforcement routes to the far north (Critical Threats).

Air power is the government's main tool: drones and Su-24 strikes on Kidal (27 May), strikes on Ouertedjach east of Aguelhok (4 Sept); the FLA cited 'disproportionate use of aerial assets' by Africa Corps for its October withdrawal.
FLA air defence capability: video of a Mi-35 downed in Gao region in April and a Mi-24 shot down at Tabrichat on 5 July 2026; a Malian Mi-24 was reportedly captured on the ground.

Anefis (4-9 July): FLA took the town in about two hours; first relief convoy from Gao intercepted at Tabrichat 55 km south; second convoy retook the town; government claimed about 30 to 80 soldiers killed (figures differ), 100+ rebels and 12 rebel vehicles destroyed.

Convoy war: the FLA's signature tactic since Anoumalane (June 2025) is ambushing long logistics convoys on desert tracks with IEDs and mobile fire teams, as on 17 July 2026 (about 50 soldiers killed, 20 captured).
6 Oct 2026 Kidal convoy: about 120 vehicles left Anefis for Kidal (about 100 km), including FAMa, Africa Corps and allied GATIA and MSA fighters; no major ground fighting reported.
Prisoner diplomacy: FLA released 82 Malian POWs on 13 Aug 2026 and about 60 more in late August in exchange for one of its generals; the FLA had claimed 200+ soldiers captured at Kidal in April.
casualties: No consolidated toll. Claims: FLA said several dozen Malian soldiers killed and 200+ captured at Kidal (April); Africa Corps claimed 1,000+ insurgents killed across Mali in the April offensive, including 200 at Kidal and 500 at Gao (unverified, includes JNIM); Anefis: government said about 30 soldiers killed and 60 wounded (Wikipedia infobox says about 80) and 100+ rebels; 17 July ambush: about 50 soldiers killed (RFI). The 'high' rating is an estimate: combined FLA-JNIM northern fighting and air strikes in April-October 2026 plausibly exceeded 1,000 deaths, but FLA-only deaths cannot be separated from JNIM's.
displaced: No figures for northern Mali displacement in 2026 were found in the sources retrieved.

timeline.event: Background: FLA ambush at Anoumalane kills about 45 Malian and Russian personnel.
FLA and JNIM seize Kidal and much of Gao.
Africa Corps confirms withdrawal from Kidal; Aguelhok and Tessalit also evacuated.
FLA and JNIM take the Tessalit military base.
Malian drones and Su-24s bomb Kidal.
FLA renews offensive and takes most of Anefis.
Relief convoy routed at Tabrichat; Mi-24 shot down.
FAMa and Africa Corps retake Anefis.
FLA ambushes convoy returning from Anefis; about 50 soldiers killed.
FLA announces strategic withdrawal; FAMa and Africa Corps enter Kidal.

outlook: Watch whether the FLA returns to convoy ambushes on the Anefis-Kidal and Gao-Kidal roads now that government lines are longer, whether Tessalit and Aguelhok are retaken, how JNIM reacts in the north, and whether Algeria resumes mediation. Possible friction between the FLA and JNIM over governance, and between JNIM and ISSP around Tessit and Menaka, are also key.

zones.note: Gao city largely rebel-held on 25 April while FAMa kept the airport; Bourem base overrun in April.

battles.name: Malian recapture of Kidal
sides: Malian Armed Forces, Africa Corps, GATIA, MSA
battles.outcome: Government reoccupation after FLA 'strategic and controlled withdrawal'; no major ground combat.
battles.forces: About 120-vehicle convoy from Anefis (about 100 km) with Africa Corps air support.
battles.significance: Restores the junta's symbolic hold on the rebel capital, but analysts call it symbolic rather than decisive and the FLA preserved its forces.

battles.name: Ambush of the convoy returning from Anefis
battles.place: Road south of Anefis, Gao region, Mali (coordinates approximate)
battles.forces: Returning FAMa-Africa Corps convoy; FLA ambush teams.
battles.losses: About 50 soldiers killed and 20 captured (RFI via Wikipedia); 2026 in Mali lists more than 50 soldiers and Africa Corps killed.
battles.significance: One of the deadliest ambushes on government forces in the north, reinforcing that convoys are the weak point.

battles.name: Battle of Anefis
battles.place: Anefis and Tabrichat, Kidal and Gao regions, Mali
battles.outcome: Inconclusive: government retook Anefis town on 9 July but FLA held surrounding terrain and the Tabrichat area.
battles.forces: FLA mobile columns; two FAMa-Africa Corps relief convoys from Gao with Mi-24 helicopter support.
battles.losses: Government claim: about 30 soldiers killed (infobox: about 80) and 60 wounded; 100+ rebels and 12 rebel vehicles destroyed; one Mi-24 shot down.
battles.significance: Showed the FLA could take a town in hours and down helicopters, and that government control of bases did not extend to the roads between them.

battles.name: Fall of Kidal and the northern collapse
battles.outcome: FLA-JNIM victory: negotiated Malian-Russian withdrawal from Kidal (26-27 Apr), then from Aguelhok and Tessalit; Tessalit base taken 1 May.
battles.forces: FLA and JNIM fighters (Africa Corps claimed 10,000-12,000 nationally); Malian garrison and Africa Corps in the former MINUSMA camp.
battles.losses: FLA claimed several dozen soldiers killed and 200+ captured; Africa Corps claimed 200 insurgents killed at Kidal (both unverified).
battles.significance: Reversed Russia's signature 2023 victory and pushed the state out of most of the far north for over five months.
